title: Measurement: the ordered setup command's first slice runs D26's order, keeps its pre-install graph to Node built-ins, installs locked dependencies without lifecycle scripts, and fixes ignore coverage inside the planned transaction
summary: TSK-0060 SLICE 1, toward ACC-0083 and — not yet evaluated — ACC-0085, ACC-0043, ACC-0045, ACC-0106, ACC-0107, ACC-0108. The implementation is commit e808b96 with its two review fixes in 7ef9d4d; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. WHAT THE COMMAND DOES, IN D26'S ORDER. `node .planning/bin/setup.mjs` resolves and prints five paths (tool root, project root, content root, settings, runtime state) before it mutates anything, refusing a --project-root that disagrees with the resolved content owner and printing both; validates this runtime against the checkout's engines.node; takes the single setup lock in the project root and holds it for the whole run; installs this checkout's locked dependencies; dynamically imports the state library, the initializer, the ignore owner and the journal's schema validator; decides state coverage by rendering the state library's own three choices; then builds the transaction plan and runs its phases — state-coverage when a fix was chosen, initialize, state-protection, project-identity — and only then opens the journal, which lives in the directory those phases have just protected and created, and sets the resume command. On success the journal is removed, so a completed run leaves nothing to recover from. ACC-0083, THE PRE-INSTALL IMPORT GRAPH. The command's static import graph is walked from bin/setup.mjs through every relative import, transitively: 8 node: built-ins and 14 Kiln modules, reaching the initializer, the ignore owner, the scaffold, the stages and the transaction — no installed package at any depth. The check is itself checked: a file with a top-level `import Ajv from "ajv/dist/2020.js"` and one with `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` are both caught, so a scan that found nothing because it looks for nothing would fail. Everything the command needs after the install — Ajv through lib/runtime-records.mjs, the state library, the initializer, the ignore owner — is imported dynamically, after the install step. THE BOOTSTRAP INSTALL. It is `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, spawned through this process's npm_execpath when there is one and the platform's npm otherwise, with cwd set to the tool root. `ci` refuses a lockfile that is missing or disagrees with package.json BEFORE it changes anything, which is the check the lockfile digest could only make afterwards; --ignore-scripts keeps dependency install lifecycle scripts from running. The digest of package-lock.json is still taken before and after, and a change is a refusal. In the tests the install is a seam that captures the project tree at the moment it ran: the consumer project was byte-identical to its pre-run state, and the five paths had already been printed. THE COVERAGE FIX IS A PLANNED WRITE INSIDE THE TRANSACTION. The operator is asked before the transaction, because deciding only reads; the write that answer authorises is `.gitignore` NAMED IN THE TRANSACTION'S FILES — so it gets the containment check, the identity recorded before anything is written and the writeability probe that every planned target gets — performed in a declared `state-coverage` phase, placed first because every later phase writes into the paths it protects. It is planned only when a fix was chosen, so an already-covered project keeps the file out of the transaction entirely. The ignore owner keeps the write, because it appends against a read taken at the moment of writing and a whole-file merge would destroy whatever reached the file in between; what makes that write planned rather than merely permitted is that the owner asks the LEDGER whether this exact file is in the plan, and refuses as `not-planned` when it is not. After a write that changed the file, the plan entry is updated from the file itself, so the journal's fileIdentities describe what is there rather than what was there before the append. THAT ADOPTION IS RESTRICTED TO `.gitignore`, because it replaces the identity `merge` compares against: offered for any planned target it would take whatever another process had just written to a merged file, record it as the plan's own, and let the next merge pass the concurrent-edit check that exists to refuse exactly that. Measured with a concurrent edit to a planned `.pi/settings.json`: adoption refuses as not-self-written, the merge that follows still refuses as concurrent-edit, and the other process's bytes survive untouched. MEASURED: a malformed .pi/kiln.json makes the plan refuse before any phase runs, and .gitignore is not written at all; inside a transaction open over that very project but with no such target planned, the write is refused and the file is not created; a transaction that planned the file for another project is refused; a forged lease and a finished transaction write nothing; the journal's own target is not adoptable and the planned list is frozen; with no transaction the owner still writes, which is the initializer's path. WHAT ELSE WAS MEASURED. A project id is minted once and reused on the next run, and the journal is gone when setup completes. A rerun with the same inputs changes no byte of what setup owns, including the mtime of .pi/kiln.json. A missing-coverage project is shown the state library's three options with the exact bytes of the block; answering nothing, `stop`, `user-state` or nonsense stops with nothing written; a --non-interactive run refuses on the same object and writes no content, no runtime state and no ignore file. An interrupted bootstrap leaves the consumer project untouched with no journal to resume, and the next run completes. A runtime below engines.node refuses before the install. LIMITS. This is one slice. --local-state user refuses by name: an external user-local root is keyed by the committed project id, which this command cannot print before the install, so ACC-0085 is deliberately NOT evaluated until every supported state path is implemented. The slice does not register the package, verify the Pi version, write the skill-override entry, ask for consent, discover or select a model, run the preflight canary or the live model check, read anything back, or map exit codes beyond the classes it can reach; ACC-0106, ACC-0107, ACC-0108, ACC-0043 and ACC-0045 are spanning criteria and stay not-evaluated until the later slices land and the integration record is written. `state-coverage` being a DECLARED PHASE rather than merely inside the transaction body is not observable in this slice: the journal opens after the last phase and is removed on success, so no run here can be caught mid-phase. Its mutation is the one that survives. No provider, network or npm registry was reached: the install is a seam in every test. CI. GitHub Actions run 35769970463 at 39c422f, attempt 1 with no job re-run, passed in all four cells, with the setup command's 13 tests, the ignore owner's 54 and the transaction's 33 running in every cell; the live compatibility tier ran in the ubuntu Node 24 cell and passed 6 of 6. The two earlier runs on this slice's code also passed all four cells: 35764251227 at e808b96 and 35767341949 at 7ef9d4d. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Twenty-five changes across four sets, each restored byte-identical by sha256. Twenty-four were caught: paths printed after the install, a project-root disagreement ignored, the runtime check skipped, a rewritten lockfile tolerated, the coverage refusal skipped, a non-interactive run answering its own question, the transaction not reusing the held lock, lock reuse without opting in (caught by test/initialize-project.test.mjs), an identity minted every run, the coverage fix applied before the plan again, the install unlocked back to `npm install`, the ignore owner's lease not authenticated, the command planning no write to .gitignore, the owner not checking the plan, the plan not told what was written, an unplanned path adopted, the planned list handed out unfrozen, the journal's own target counted as planned, any planned target adoptable, the self-written file named as .pi/settings.json, and adoption skipping the plan. THE ONE THAT SURVIVES is running the coverage fix inside the transaction body but outside a declared phase, for the reason stated above: the journal opens after the last phase and is removed on success, so no run in this slice can be caught mid-phase.

facts.implementation: commits e808b96acf7146d98f32cc8765b68ab4846c7580 (slice 1), 7ef9d4d (F2 and F3), 39c422f (F2 corrected: .gitignore planned as a target) and 7ff2fc2 (adoption restricted to that target)
facts.tests: test/setup-command.test.mjs: 13 tests, all running the real main() against a temporary Git repository with two seams (npm and the operator's answer). test/project-gitignore.test.mjs: 54 tests, one of them the planned-target rule. test/setup-transaction.test.mjs: 34 tests, three of them the planned list, adoptPlannedWrite and the concurrent edit it must not launder.
facts.acc-0083-graph: walked from bin/setup.mjs through every relative import, transitively: 8 node: built-ins (async_hooks, child_process, crypto, fs, os, path, readline, url) and 14 Kiln modules — activation, atomic-write, content-root, content-version, dependency-freshness, initialize-project, lock, project-gitignore, project-scaffold, setup-transaction, specialists/roster, stage-documents, stages, tool-wire-names — and zero installed packages at any depth
facts.acc-0083-self-check: a file importing ajv/dist/2020.js and a file importing @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent are both caught by the same scan
facts.install-arguments: npm ci --ignore-scripts, cwd = tool root, through npm_execpath when set and npm/npm.cmd otherwise; asserted on both paths
facts.install-confinement: at the moment the install ran, the consumer project tree was byte-identical to its pre-run state and the five paths had been printed
facts.lockfile: package-lock.json digest taken before and after; a rewrite is EXIT.INSTALL with nothing of the project changed
facts.coverage-fix-planned: the command plans .gitignore as a transaction target when a coverage fix was chosen, and not otherwise; the owner refuses a transaction that did not plan it. A malformed .pi/kiln.json is refused at plan time: exit 7, no .gitignore written, no content written, and the malformed record itself unchanged
facts.ignore-owner-lease: a forged lease, a transaction open over this project that did not plan the file, a transaction that planned it for another project, and a finished transaction each refuse and write nothing; with no transaction the owner still writes
facts.identity: minted once (32 hex characters), reused on the next run, journal absent after success
facts.rerun: byte-identical tree on a second run, and .pi/kiln.json keeps its mtime on a third
facts.non-interactive: refuses with the state library's own options and writes no .pi, no content and no .gitignore
facts.interrupted-bootstrap: consumer project unchanged, no .pi directory, no journal; the next run completes
facts.mutations: 25 run locally on Windows across four sets, 24 killed, 1 survives (a declared phase is not observable in this slice); each restored byte-identical by sha256
facts.full-suite-local: npm test on Windows: 1573 tests, 1568 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped
facts.locked-install-resolves: npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run in this checkout: 'up to date', so package-lock.json and package.json agree and the real bootstrap resolves
facts.ci-run: GitHub Actions run 35769970463 at 39c422f, attempt 1, no job re-run, all four cells succeeded, 0 failures in any cell; runs 35764251227 (e808b96) and 35767341949 (7ef9d4d) passed all four cells earlier in the slice
facts.live-tier: ubuntu-latest Node 24 cell only (job 106888919037), KILN_PI_COMPAT=live: 6 of 6 pass; skipped in the other three cells
facts.planned-write-record: adoptPlannedWrite updates the plan entry from the file after a write that changed it, so the journal's fileIdentities match what is there; it is restricted to the project's .gitignore and refuses every other planned target as not-self-written, as well as an unplanned path, the journal's own target and a finished transaction, and it reads the identity from disk rather than from its caller
facts.adoption-cannot-launder: with a concurrent edit to a planned .pi/settings.json: adoption refuses, tx.merge still refuses as concurrent-edit, and the other process's bytes are unchanged

omissions.reason: npm is a seam in every test: spawning it would install a dependency graph per case. What is asserted is the exact argument list on both npm paths, the cwd, the lockfile digest either side, and that the project tree was untouched when the install ran.
--local-state user refuses by name in this slice, so ACC-0085 is not evaluated until every supported state path is implemented.
The journal opens after the last phase and is removed on success, so no run in this slice can be caught mid-phase. Running the coverage fix outside a declared phase is the one mutation that survives.

Package registration, the Pi version check, the skill-override entry, consent, model discovery and selection, the preflight canary, the live model check, read-back and the full exit-code mapping are slices 2 to 4. The spanning criteria stay not-evaluated until the integration record.
